reference: Metadata expectations use GNU Bash's documented type/help builtins and the published su usage/help contract. The util-linux su executable is not a safe or equivalent oracle for this builtin: its operations authenticate against host account services and change process identity, while bash-os su uses a kernel auth token. No operation parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash reports su as a registered builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented su invocation, password model, and kernel-token description.
Deferred operation coverage identifies parser, account-file, authentication, token, privilege-transition, child-execution, and terminal requirements for a disposable VM or injected mock.
exclusions: No su operation invocation is run. Authentication, token authorization, credential changes, target-shell execution, and PTY behavior require controlled private fixtures or a disposable VM.
No host account, password, shadow file, authorization device, or installed credential is accessed.
No GNU/util-linux su comparison is run because it would use host authentication and identity-changing behavior and does not implement the bash-os token contract.

cases.purpose: Verify that Bash resolves su as a builtin using the documented type -t metadata contract, without invoking su.

Check that the registered help text contains the declared invocation form and documented password and auth-token descriptions. The fixed marker is emitted only when all documented anchors are present.
cases.script:
PATH=
help su >help.txt
want_usage='su [--login|--no-login] [--keep-env] [-c CMD] [USER]'
usage=0
description=0
password=0
token=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  case $line in
    *"$want_usage"*) usage=1 ;;
    *'Switch user with C-owned password verification.'*) description=1 ;;
    *'Argon2id PHC shadow format used by passwd.'*) password=1 ;;
    *'short-lived kernel auth token is minted and consumed internally'*) token=1 ;;
  esac
done <help.txt
[[ $usage == 1 && $description == 1 && $password == 1 && $token == 1 ]]
printf 'help contract anchors present\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise option parsing, default target selection, --, -c forms, extra arguments, invalid names, and exit/diagnostic behavior.
Check account lookup for present, absent, malformed, and unreadable synthetic passwd records, including target UID/GID/home/shell selection.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: The test uses only the same uid/gid 2000, so it does not establish selection among varying target IDs or a real credential transition.

cases.purpose: Check correct and incorrect passwords, locked or malformed shadow entries, bounded password input, failure lockout, and success cleanup.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: The correct project-style synthetic credential reached mock MINT/CONSUME; real token authority and credential transition were not exercised.; r3: Not executed.; r4: Not executed.; r5: The saved lock state and expiry handling were observed, but the expired-path su command subsequently failed at setgroups; a successful final credential transition was not shown.

cases.purpose: Check token mint/consume request fields, expiry, failure handling, and request cleanup before any credential transition.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r2: Synthetic consume preceded an intercepted setgroups denial; no real token enforcement or successful credential transition occurred.; r3: Injected mint, consume and expiry errors aborted before observed credential calls; real kernel token expiry and enforcement were not exercised.; r4: Observable now via the PTY password path (correct password -> 'kernel auth: /dev/bashos-auth: No such file or directory', status 1, no target shell marker).

cases.purpose: Check supplementary groups and ordered setgroups/setresgid/setresuid transitions, saved-ID verification, and denial on each injected failure.
cases.reason: The transition runs only after the kernel token (both root and non-root routes call bsu_kernel_proof) and needs privilege. Blocked by guest /dev/bashos-auth v2 UAPI implementation (kernel module or a root-owned CUSE character-device mock implementing loadables/common/_bashos_auth_uapi.h: VERSION, PRIVCMD_AUTHZ, EXEC_VERIFY, EXEC_HANDOFF, token mint/consume, secret slots, policy info). The Debian guest kernel has no such device and the repository holds only the UAPI header, so open() fails with ENOENT and no unprivileged fixture can observe any ioctl behaviour and guest case option to run a side as uid 0 inside a private mount namespace with fixture /etc/passwd and /etc/group bind-mounted (guest.py terminal.child_limits always drops to uid 2000; a drop to a second synthetic uid needs CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID, the legacy runner disables user namespaces, and an unprivileged user namespace maps only one uid); failure injection additionally needs syscall errno/short-count injection for a static binary (seccomp SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO or user-notify filter installed by a trusted guest helper, matched on fd/pid/syscall).

cases.purpose: Check login and no-login argv, working directory, filtered and retained environment, descriptor closure, and exec errors using a controlled target shell.
Check child exit and signal status propagation, fork/wait errors, parent-shell state preservation, and repeated invocation behavior.
Check tty password echo suppression and terminal restoration after success, read failure, and cancellation.
